lines.text: One team went to a World Cup, faced the champions of the world, and never lost a single game.
And still went home. Tonight that team walks out again — and in the stands, an old man keeps an impossible record alive.
Last time, we predicted Uruguay would beat Saudi Arabia two-one. Tonight, two underdogs with everything to prove.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode twenty. Iran versus New Zealand. Team Melli... against the All Whites.
And stay with me — because the secret in this one is the strangest unbeaten run in World Cup history.
First, the history. And this one is true. South Africa, twenty ten. New Zealand — ranked near the bottom of the whole tournament.
Game one, against Slovakia. Ninety-third minute, losing — and Winston Reid rises to head it in. One-all. Their first ever World Cup point.
Game two: the defending world champions, Italy. New Zealand score first, and hold on. One-all. The tiny nation refuses to fall.
Game three, Paraguay. Nil-nil. Three games, three draws — and not a single defeat.
They went home unbeaten. The only team at the entire World Cup that never lost. And Italy, the champions? Out — bottom of the group.
Across the pitch tonight — Iran. Team Melli, with their own piece of World Cup folklore.
France, nineteen ninety-eight. In a match heavy with politics, Iran beat the United States two-one — their first ever win at a World Cup.
Yet here is the ache they share: in all their history, Iran have never once escaped the group. Two nations chasing the same door.
Iran. Led by Mehdi Taremi — the man they call the Iranian Ronaldo, who once worked a gas station before football gave him a second life.
Beside him, Alireza Jahanbakhsh, the captain who went to Europe and came back a leader. Saman Ghoddos pulling the strings.
And the steel behind them — Saeid Ezatolahi shielding the back, Mehdi Ghaedi running at tired legs. Disciplined, organised, hungry.
New Zealand. The All Whites — and up top, a giant. Chris Wood, the Auckland boy who became his country's greatest ever scorer.
Around him: Marko Stamenic driving midfield, Liberato Cacace flying down the left, Barbarouses and Sarpreet Singh chasing more history.
So here is the duel. Iran's discipline against New Zealand's heart. Taremi's craft... against Wood's power.
Our prediction — built on two proud underdogs who hate to lose, and a knockout place hanging on every touch. Watch.
Iran press first. Ghoddos slides it wide, the cross hangs — and Taremi attacks it, that classic centre-forward's leap. One-nil, Iran.
But you do not tell the unbeaten team it's over. New Zealand come, all white shirts and broad shoulders.
Cacace whips it in from the left — and the giant climbs. Chris Wood, of course. One-all.
One apiece at the whistle, in our story. Team Melli's craft, the All Whites' refusal to lose. Two underdogs, level, both still standing.
Do you agree? Comment TEAM MELLI if Iran finally break through. Comment ALL WHITES if New Zealand stay unbeaten again.
And the old man with the record? Legend number twenty: the Unbeaten.
He was in South Africa in twenty ten — saw all three draws — and he's never once seen his All Whites lose at a World Cup. He keeps that flame burning. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings us to YOU. At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score scores for you.
